To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a patient with bilateral ANs, NF2, and preserved DPOAE.
1) The patient had a complete bilateral neural deafness.
1. In a patient with NF2, bilateral acoustic neuromata were found.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the function of the cochlea in acoustic neurinoma.
the question whether the DPOAE is a useful parameter for the diagnosis of acoustic neurinoma with intact OHC.
the question of whether there is a possibility of hearing preservation after surgery of acoustic neuromas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DPOAEs were generated by the OHC, but not by the AN.
in the case of a patient with NF2 and a bilateral acoustic neurinoma, the hearing loss is caused by the tumour and not by the NF2 itself.
the OHCs are still functioning but are disconnected from the neural input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DPOAE are not only a measure of the OHC function but also a measure of the neural integrity.
the DPOAE are not a measure for the cochlear function, but for OHC function.
the cochlea is a complex organ and that the function of OHC and IHC is not the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DPOAE are a good predictor of hearing preservation in acoustic neuroma surgery.
DPOAE are a useful tool to detect residual function in AN patients.
the patient had a very rare audiologic constellation with preserved OHC function despite bilateral neural deafness.
